headline: The Thunder year starts high in October and peaks in April and May
summary: No other pro team competes for a Wednesday night in Oklahoma City, so the whole state shows up, in the arena and in retail data. Football, storm season and the Women's College World Series shape the calendar around the playoffs. This year's title co-favorite opens at San Antonio, where its West finals run ended. Demand clusters around opening night, Christmas, the playoff run and the days after a series win.

insights.title: Watch parties run far from Bricktown
insights.detail: With no NFL, MLB or NHL team in the state, the Thunder carry Oklahoma's whole pro-sports identity. Fans drive in from Tulsa, Lawton, Norman and Stillwater, and watch parties run far from Bricktown.
insights.implication: Plan drops and pop-ups beyond OKC: Tulsa, Norman, Stillwater and the tribal casino-resort markets. Ship product as "Oklahoma" as well as "OKC".

insights.title: Football owns the fall, and fans wear both
insights.detail: October and November belong to OU and OSU football (crimson/cream and orange). The Oct 20 opener and the Friday Cup games land mid-week or on Friday nights, so attention is shared. Many households split between Sooners and Cowboys, but all of them are Thunder.
insights.implication: Stay out of the Saturday football window. Make Thunder blue the shared color, and skip crimson or orange blocking that reads as a college rival.

insights.title: Spring playoffs are the civic peak
insights.detail: In the playoff months the city turns out in blue for "Loud City" games, with watch parties at the Paycom Center plaza and in Bricktown. After a West finals loss, fans expect a deep run, and a series win changes retail demand within 24 hours.
insights.implication: Hold inventory and graphics capacity for a fast-turn playoff drop from mid-April: T-shirts, hoodies and series-specific pieces. Anchor everything in Thunder blue and sunset orange. Fans buy proof of belonging.

insights.title: Weather sets the apparel calendar
insights.detail: Oklahoma summers are hot and long, and spring brings severe weather. Fall and winter are short and variable, with cold snaps and ice storms. Spring tornado watches change game-night routines: the arena has policies, and fans watch with weather alerts on.
insights.implication: Layer up from October to April with hoodies, warm-ups and lightweight windbreakers. Cover the June to September gap with breathable tees. A wind- and storm-ready outer layer fits the state's identity.

insights.title: The Cup matters more than Christmas
insights.detail: The Dec 25 game is at Minnesota (8:00 p.m. ET). There's no home Christmas party, but it's a national-TV moment and a gift-buying peak. The NBA Cup Friday games (West Group B with MIN, LAC, NOP, MEM) turn November into a mini-playoff for OKC fans. In December the Cup knockout can bring a home semifinal if OKC is the higher seed.
insights.implication: Treat Black Friday to Dec 25 as the biggest gift window. Build court-inspired Cup pieces for group play. Holiday giving skews to jerseys, hoodies and youth sizes.

insights.title: Offseason is quiet, but the draft is real
insights.detail: July to September drops sharply. The exceptions are Summer League, the state fair in September and football kickoff. The Thunder's draft capital makes late June a lively window for fan talk, and Presti's moves get discussed like a civic project.
insights.implication: Use the quiet months for launches aimed at long-lead buyers (youth, collectors), city-specific graphics and a City Edition reveal buildup. Skip the hard sell.

places.name: Paycom Center
places.why: The home arena and the center of the Loud City ritual. Every watch party and drop points here.

places.name: Bricktown
places.why: Brick warehouses and a canal, a short walk from the arena. It has the biggest bar and restaurant crowds before and after games.

places.name: Scissortail Park
places.why: A downtown park with a large lawn, used for festivals and community events. A natural summer pop-up site.

places.name: Deep Deuce
places.why: The historic Black jazz and cultural district, tied to Ralph Ellison and Charlie Christian. Community partners should lead any local-heritage story told here.

places.name: Plaza District
places.why: Indie shops, murals and the monthly arts crawl. It has the strongest local-maker and streetwear energy in town.

places.name: Paseo Arts District
places.why: Spanish-revival buildings and studios, and home to First Friday Gallery Walks.

places.name: Devon Park (USA Softball Hall of Fame Stadium)
places.why: Home of the Women's College World Series in early June, which overlaps with the end of the NBA season.

places.name: Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium
places.why: OU football sets the fall sports calendar that the Thunder compete and combine with.

people.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
people.why: The face of the franchise and of the city's identity. Fans track his style, from suits to tunnel fits.

people.name: Chet Holmgren
people.why: The second pillar of the young core, and a fan favorite for his rim protection and 7-foot guard skills.

people.name: Jalen Williams
people.why: Core scorer and creator, nicknamed "J-Dub" by fans and a major jersey seller.

people.name: Sam Presti
people.role: Thunder executive vice president and general manager
people.why: Architect of the roster and the draft strategy fans trust. Quoted as saying he will not cut payroll to dodge the tax.

people.name: Mark Daigneault
people.why: His development-first approach defines how the team plays and how fans talk about it.

people.name: Aday Mara
people.why: A new face for 2026-27 and a likely first-year jersey and tee story.

moments.name: Oklahoma City Memorial Marathon
moments.why: The city's biggest civic ritual, held in remembrance of the 1995 bombing. It overlaps with the first playoff round, so keep the tone respectful.

moments.name: Festival of the Arts
moments.why: A multi-day downtown arts festival that fills the streets just as the playoffs start.

moments.name: Women's College World Series
moments.why: OKC's softball showcase, with huge crowds and national attention during the NBA Finals window.

moments.name: Oklahoma State Fair
moments.why: The state's biggest fall gathering, and a pre-season tie-in for casual fans.

moments.name: OU-Texas Red River Rivalry
moments.why: The state's biggest football weekend. It soaks up sports attention just before NBA opening night.

moments.name: Opening night at San Antonio
moments.why: A West finals rematch on NBC/Peacock, and the first emotional peak of the season.

moments.name: Plaza District Festival and arts walks
moments.why: A year-round way into the local-maker scene for community collaborations.

vocabulary.meaning: The fan identity built on the arena's noise, used on signs, shirts and social posts.
The team's rally call and hashtag, used by fans and the team.
Fans' nickname for the arena from its Chesapeake Energy Arena days. Some still use it casually.
The OU-OSU rivalry, used for football and other sports. It's the state's other great sports frame.
Shorthand for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, used on shirts and in chants.
Fans' shorthand for OU and OSU. Many households are split.

designCues.cue: Thunder blue as the dominant field
designCues.source: The team's primary color, seen in the arena every game.
designCues.use: Use it as the main color on playoff-run and season-long product. It unites fans across college loyalties.

designCues.source: The team's secondary accent, tied to the horizon over the plains.
designCues.use: Use it as trim and accent, and keep it away from OSU's orange territory in the fall.

designCues.source: Thunder navy and yellow (#FDBB30) from the team palette.
designCues.use: Use it for cold-weather layering pieces and premium trims.

designCues.source: Oklahoma's big skies, storm fronts and lightning, which tie to the Thunder name.
designCues.use: Use a tone-on-tone sky gradient or lightning line on hoodies and warm-ups. Keep it abstract, not literal weather-warning imagery.

designCues.source: Bricktown's red-brick warehouses and the canal.
designCues.use: Use a tonal brick pattern or heathered texture for a downtown-district capsule.

designCues.source: Oklahoma wind, cold snaps and ice storms from October to April.
designCues.use: Use it for windbreakers and shell jackets aimed at fall and spring game nights.

productHooks: Playoff fast-turn capsule: blue-first tees, hoodies and warm-up tops with "Loud City" or series graphics, ready to ship within 48 hours of a series win.
Fall layering collection for Oct to Dec: quarter-zips, hoodies and shell jackets in Thunder blue and navy, timed to opening night and holiday gifting.
NBA Cup Friday-night pieces for West Group B play, tied to the Cup court look and sold in November.
Statewide Oklahoma capsule sold in Tulsa and Norman, built on state-shape and plains-sky graphics, not city-only logos.
watchouts: Keep imagery of the 1995 bombing and the Memorial out of commercial graphics. Keep spring marketing respectful around the Memorial Marathon.
OU and OSU marks, colors and Bedlam are licensed. Avoid crimson/cream or orange blocking that could imply a college affiliation.
Use Native nations' designs and sacred imagery only through partnership, credit and payment to tribal artists.
Avoid storm or tornado imagery that could read as trivializing real disasters.

team: MLK Day games Jan 18 (OKC game not confirmed)
months.fanBehavior: Steady home-game attendance. Fans start tracking seeding and MVP talk.
months.retailSignal: Post-holiday gift cards and sales. Hoodies and warm-ups sell.

months.fanBehavior: Deadline chatter and All-Star voting for Gilgeous-Alexander and company. Engagement is high but passive.
months.retailSignal: All-Star and player-focused tees sell. Team-wide demand is quieter.

team: Seeding race for the West No. 1 seed
months.fanBehavior: Attention builds toward the playoffs and splits with March Madness.
months.retailSignal: Lighter layers and early playoff-gear teasers.

months.phase: Season end, Play-In and playoffs begin
months.fanBehavior: The city turns blue, watch parties return and casual fans come back.
months.retailSignal: Playoff tees and shirts spike on series wins.

team: Second round and West finals if the team advances
months.fanBehavior: Peak intensity and noise. Schools, businesses and restaurants show blue. This peak assumes a deep run.
months.retailSignal: Demand for blue tees, hoodies and jerseys is highest, and stock-outs are a risk.

team: NBA Finals if the team advances
months.fanBehavior: Intensity depends on whether the team is still playing. If not, attention shifts to the draft and softball.
months.retailSignal: Champion or run-themed gear if the run is deep. Otherwise clearance and draft-pick tees.

months.fanBehavior: A quiet offseason. Hardcore fans follow roster and contract news.
months.retailSignal: Lightweight tees and summer sale items.

months.fanBehavior: The lowest point of the year. Fans look at the schedule and new uniforms.
months.retailSignal: Back-to-school youth apparel and schedule-release tees.

months.fanBehavior: Football dominates. Thunder interest returns with media-day content.

team: Opening night Oct 20 at San Antonio
Home opener in the week after
months.fanBehavior: Excitement builds for the West finals rematch, and fans size up the roster after the offseason trades.
months.retailSignal: Jerseys and opening-night pieces. Layering starts.

team: Cup Friday nights Oct 30 to Nov 27
months.fanBehavior: Cup games feel like mini-playoffs. Fans split their time with football.
months.retailSignal: Black Friday and early gift sales, plus Cup gear.

team: Christmas at Minnesota Dec 25, 8:00 p.m. ET
months.fanBehavior: Gift buying peaks, holiday viewing is big and casual engagement is strong.
months.retailSignal: The biggest jersey, hoodie and youth gift month of the regular season.

keyDates.name: Opening night at San Antonio
keyDates.why: A West finals rematch on NBC/Peacock at 9:30 p.m. ET, and the first peak of the season.

keyDates.name: OKC vs Denver on ESPN
keyDates.why: A national-TV game two days after the opener. An early chance for a watch-party push.

keyDates.name: NBA Cup group play begins
keyDates.why: OKC is in West Group B with MIN, LAC, NOP and MEM. Games are on Friday nights and in Thanksgiving week.

keyDates.name: NBA Cup knockouts and final
keyDates.why: Semifinals are at the higher seed's home arena. The final is at Hinkle Fieldhouse on Dec 11.

keyDates.name: Christmas Day at Minnesota
keyDates.why: 8:00 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC: a national audience and a gift-buying peak.

keyDates.name: Trade deadline
keyDates.why: Roster talk peaks, especially with the payroll near the second apron.

keyDates.name: NBA All-Star Weekend
keyDates.why: In Phoenix. Gilgeous-Alexander and teammates are likely selections.

keyDates.name: Regular season ends
keyDates.why: The Play-In and playoff window starts.

keyDates.name: Memorial Marathon
keyDates.why: A civic remembrance event that overlaps with the first round. Keep the tone respectful.

keyDates.name: Women's College World Series
keyDates.why: A large local event that overlaps with the NBA Finals window.
